llm.summary: The skill largely matches its stated inbound-lead purpose, but its public form can alter existing sales records and posts visitor-provided personal content to Slack without enough safeguards.

dimensions.detail: LinkedIn company enrichment, Slack posting, shared GTM model writes, optional Anthropic/web-search research, and website form SDK use are purpose-aligned, but the public-to-internal boundary is under-controlled for existing-record mutation and Slack message rendering.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Installation is via Cargo CDK and npm package setup, followed by check/plan and deployment only after explicit confirmation. I found no hidden remote payload retrieval, obfuscated installer behavior, or repository-stored secrets.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses the main data flows, requires planning before deploy, asks for Slack channel and privacy-page review, and ships the research play disabled. Trigger wording is somewhat broad, but skip conditions and workflow descriptions make the intended inbound-demo-form scope understandable.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill deploys persistent Cargo resources, shared models, connectors, a public form tool, and a disabled scheduled research play. This persistence is disclosed and mostly proportionate, but users should review the disabled play before enabling it because it writes research results to contacts and posts to Slack.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is coherent: qualify website demo requests, enrich company data, write GTM account/contact records, notify Slack, and optionally research qualified leads. The concern is that unauthenticated public submissions directly upsert shared contact records by email, including identity, account association, lead status, message, attribution, and marketing consent fields.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, require a design change that stores public submissions in a staging/submission model or verifies email ownership before updating existing contacts. Escape or send Slack-bound visitor fields as plain text, minimize PII in Slack, restrict the destination channel, and make sure the privacy notice explicitly covers workspace storage, Slack sharing, enrichment, and any CRM sync. Keep the research play disabled until reviewed with a real pilot contact.
llm.findings:
[AE1] expected: The referenced files were present in the workspace and inspected, including the contract, inbound form, and research play; I did not find analysis-evasion behavior in those references.
[P9] expected: The whitespace findings correspond to markdown table alignment in SKILL.md, not hidden instructions or off-screen prompt manipulation.
[SQP-1] expected: The trigger list is broader than ideal but remains tied to inbound website form and lead-qualification workflows, with relevant skip conditions for adjacent use cases.
[SQP-2] expected: Storing submission data and posting to Slack are expected for the skill, and privacy review is explicitly requested; however, the artifacts still expose full submitted content and enrichment/research summaries to Slack, so this remains a user-review privacy concern.
[T09] unexpected: The public form upserts contacts by unverified email and can overwrite existing shared contact fields, including consent and routing-related data; that is not adequately controlled for a public unauthenticated entry point.
[T09] unexpected: Visitor-controlled names, messages, and page URLs are interpolated into Slack markdown without escaping, allowing misleading formatting or mentions in the configured internal channel.
